Predict the recorded human decision in a public-goods experiment. Follow the participant instructions below; do not solve for an optimal action or explain your answer. Four people stay in the same anonymous group for 10 announced rounds. Each starts with 250 Taler and receives 20 Taler each round; 50 Taler = EUR 1. At the end, the total Taler balance is converted to euros and rounded to one decimal place, and paid in cash. Communication is prohibited.
Stage 1: all four simultaneously choose a whole-number contribution from 0 to 20 Taler. The pool is multiplied by 1.6 and divided equally. Stage-1 income is 20 minus own contribution plus 0.4 times all four contributions. Other current contributions are shown at Stage 2. Any rank information provided by this condition is shown only then.
Stage 2: each participant simultaneously assigns reduction points to each of the three other people. Each assigned point costs the sender 1 Taler. The instructions specify one Type A person and three Type B people. A point assigned by Type A removes 4 Taler from its recipient; a Type B point removes 1 Taler. Type A can assign at most 5 points to each other person; Type B at most 10. You are informed of your own type before assigning reduction points. Type A is assigned randomly in round 1. In later rounds it goes to the person with the highest cumulative income at the start of the round, with random selection among tied leaders. Your round income is stage-1 income minus the cost of your assigned points and the Taler removed by received points. You receive your own income and punishment feedback after the two stages. At Stage 2 the income ranks based on completed rounds are also shown; tied values share a rank. Anonymous numbers and display order change each round. The target_1/2/3 names below are local normalization aliases, ordered by observed contribution and, when shown, rank. They do not recover original display order or link people across rounds. Other people’s actual types and private histories are not supplied.
Return only the numeric Taler contribution, with no explanation.

In later rounds it goes to the person with the highest cumulative social status (described in the instructions as own cumulative contributions minus received reduction points) at the start of the round, with random selection among tied leaders. Your round income is stage-1 income minus the cost of your assigned points and the Taler removed by received points. You receive your own income and punishment feedback after the two stages. At Stage 2 the social-status ranks based on completed rounds are also shown; tied values share a rank. The instructions describe social status as cumulative contributions minus received reduction points. Anonymous numbers and display order change each round. Your round income is stage-1 income minus the cost of your assigned points and the Taler removed by received points. You receive your own income and punishment feedback after the two stages. At Stage 2 the social-status ranks based on completed rounds are also shown; tied values share a rank. The instructions describe social status as cumulative contributions minus received reduction points. Anonymous numbers and display order change each round.
